evaluation_question: What replenishment action should we take for LAP-103? Calculate the risk and required order quantity, apply MOQ/order-multiple constraints, and explain whether the order can arrive in time under NovaTech policy.
gold_answer: INCREASE replenishment and review an expedite/earlier-supply action. At CW+1, projected inventory = 0 and unmet demand = 11. Forward average demand = 36 units/week; 5-WOS target inventory = 180; gap = -180; raw replenishment requirement = 180 units. MOQ = 30 and order multiple = 10, so the valid adjusted order quantity remains 180 units. First stockout exposure occurs at CW+1. PO-1002 for 120 units arrives at CW+4, after stockout. A new standard order with TechSource's 6-week lead time would arrive at CW+6; arrival risk = TRUE with a 5-week timing gap.
gold_criteria: Must use CW+1 planning point; return 180 raw requirement and 180 valid order quantity; identify CW+1 stockout with 11 unmet; identify existing PO arrival at CW+4 and standard new-order arrival at CW+6; arrival risk TRUE; recommend increase plus review of expedite/earlier supply under policy

expected_policy_docs: POL-103 primary; POL-105 + POL-106 required/relevant; POL-104 relevant; POL-101 relevant for 5-WOS target

results.title: # NovaTech Retail — Lead Time, Stockout Risk & Expedite Policy
results.author: Supply Planning Operations
results.chunk_text:
A SKU may also have replenishment risk without reaching zero inventory.
Projected inventory at the replenishment arrival date should therefore also be
assessed against the inventory targets defined in POL-101.

For replenishment planning, POL-101 defines:

* Healthy inventory range: 4–6 WOS
* Standard planning target: 5 WOS
* Critical inventory: below 2 WOS
* Potential overstock: above 8 WOS

For example:

* Available inventory: 300 units
* Approved weekly forecast: 100 units
* Current WOS: 3 weeks
* Supplier lead time: 2 weeks
* No confirmed incoming supply

After two weeks of forecast demand, approximately 100 units would remain when
newly ordered supply could first become available.

The projected pre-arrival inventory position is therefore approximately 1 WOS.

results.title: # NovaTech Retail — Replenishment Decision Policy
results.author: Supply Planning Operations
results.chunk_text:
An increase should be considered when projected coverage remains below target and existing incoming supply is insufficient.

The current plan should normally be maintained when projected coverage remains healthy or confirmed incoming supply is sufficient to restore coverage.

A reduction should be considered when projected inventory creates material overstock risk.

A delay should be considered when supply remains necessary but its current arrival timing would create unnecessary excess inventory.

No replenishment action should be based on current WOS alone.

Document ID: POL-103
An increase should be considered when projected coverage remains below target and existing incoming supply is insufficient.

The current plan should normally be maintained when projected coverage remains healthy or confirmed incoming supply is sufficient to restore coverage.

A reduction should be considered when projected inventory creates material overstock risk.

A delay should be considered when supply remains necessary but its current arrival timing would create unnecessary excess inventory.

No replenishment action should be based on current WOS alone.

results.title: # NovaTech Retail — Lead Time, Stockout Risk & Expedite Policy
results.author: Supply Planning Operations
results.chunk_text:
A SKU may require replenishment action even when no stockout is projected if its
future inventory position remains below the planning target defined in POL-101.

An expedite should be considered when standard or confirmed supply cannot arrive
in time to prevent a material inventory gap.

Critical or below-target WOS does not automatically require an expedite.

The core planning assessment therefore considers both:

1. whether sufficient supply will arrive before inventory is exhausted; and
2. what the projected inventory position will be when that supply becomes
   available.

These conditions must be evaluated using the approved planning data and
inventory targets applicable to the SKU.
